extracted.intended_audience: aspiring poets, dramatists, and writers of verse
extracted.subtask_description: Practical prescriptive rules for composing poetry and drama (Horace's Ars Poetica): emphasis on wisdom, craft, plausibility, revision, audience, and moral/instructional purpose. Advice aimed at producing durable, effective verse rather than careless or merely fashionable pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wisdom (thought) before words
rubrics_metrics.description: "Of writing well, be sure, the secret lies In wisdom: therefore study to be wise."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary requirement is sound thought and moral/sentimental comprehension; study philosophers and life (Plato, duties to country, parent, friend) so that 'the words will come as soon as sought.' A play devoid of beauty yet with fitting thoughts and morals will engage readers more than clever verse without thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe life and manners for 'living words'
rubrics_metrics.description: "Look too to life and manners, as they lie Before you: these will living words supply."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use direct observation of people, social roles, and conduct as the source of natural expression and appropriate sentiment for characters and parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concision and economy of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: "Whene'er you lecture, be concise: the soul Takes in short maxims, and retains them whole: But pour in water when the vessel's filled, It simply dribbles over and is spilled."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer short, memorable statements; avoid overloading a passage with material after its point is made. Overstuffing dilutes effect — stop when the audience's capacity is reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verisimilitude / internal plausibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "Keep near to truth in a fictitious piece, Nor treat belief as matter of caprice. If on a child you make a vampire sup, It must not be alive when she's ripped up."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain internal consistency and plausible cause/effect even in fiction or fantastical plots; do not violate the story's own rules in ways that break readers' belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine instruction with pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: "But he who, mixing grave and gay, can teach And yet give pleasure, gains a vote from each:"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to instruct (moral, civic lessons) while entertaining; work that both amuses and teaches reaches wider audiences, sells and endures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occasional slips excused; repeated faults condemned
rubrics_metrics.description: "Some faults may claim forgiveness... But the copyist who keeps stumbling still At the same word had best lay down his quill: The harp-player, who for ever wounds the ear With the same discord, makes the audience jeer:"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single lapses or careless blots can be forgiven; systematic, repeated errors (same awkward phrasing, recurring technical mistake) mark incompetence and should be eliminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different works find readers differently (immediate vs. slow appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Some poems, like some paintings, take the eye Best at a distance, some when looked at nigh... One pleases straightway; one, when it has passed Ten times before the mind, will please at last."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that reception varies: some pieces are instantly pleasing, others require repeated exposure. This affects expectations for immediate popularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mediocrity — small fails are total fails
rubrics_metrics.description: "gods, and men, and booksellers agree To place their ban on middling poetry... If by an inch you fail, you fail outright."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Middling work is rejected by readers and market alike. Strive for clear excellence; half-success or near-miss will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talent must be married to art (learned craft)
rubrics_metrics.description: "For me, I cannot see how native wit Can e'er dispense with art, or art with it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural genius alone is insufficient; technique, learning, and practiced rules are necessary. Train craft even if naturally gifted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline, rehearsal and preparation before public performance
rubrics_metrics.description: "The youth who suns for prizes wisely trains, Bears cold and heat, is patient and abstains: The flute-player at a festival, before He plays in public, has to learn his lore."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop stamina and discipline — practice under hardship, rehearse thoroughly, and do not expect to perform well without dedicated preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against mercenary motives and corrupting patronage
rubrics_metrics.description: "O, when this cankering rust, this greed of gain, Has touched the soul and wrought into its grain, What hope that poets will produce such lines..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing for profit or flattering patrons leads to degraded work. Beware the corrupting influence of wealth, market pressure, or writing solely to please buyers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not trust flattery; prefer honest severe criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: "Don't ask a man whose feelings overflow... He'll cry, 'Good! bravo! exquisite indeed!'... A wise and faithful counsellor will blame Weak verses, note the rough, condemn the lame..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek critics who will correct defects rather than flatter. False praise masks faults; a candid, demanding friend/censor improves work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold back early drafts; revise thoroughly before release
rubrics_metrics.description: "Entrust it first to Maecius' critic ears, Your sire's, and mine, and keep it back nine years. What's kept at home you cancel by a stroke: What's sent abroad you never can revoke."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay publication until a work is polished; private revision allows cancellation and correction that public release does not. Be cautious and revise repeatedly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match sentiment/tone to theatrical role and part
rubrics_metrics.description: "That man, when need occurs, will soon invent For every part its proper sentiment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each role or part has an appropriate emotional register and diction; sentiments must fit character and dramatic function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat public/known subjects with care; originality risks offence
rubrics_metrics.description: "Than alter facts and characters, and tell In a strange form the tale men know so well... It is hard to treat hackneyed subjects with originality."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With well-known stories or public materials, either reproduce faithfully or follow strict artistic rules when attempting novelty; reckless alteration may alienate audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of hired audiences and manufactured praise
rubrics_metrics.description: "As puffing auctioneers collect a throng, Rich poets bribe false friends to hear their song... Hired mourners at a funeral say and do A little more than they whose grief is true:"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not equate crowd noise or paid applause with genuine merit. Evaluate response from impartial observers rather than assembled flatterers.
